title: Search results, Smart Folders and Recents update when files change on disk
problem: 0.5.1 made every folder on screen follow changes from other programs, but a result list never does. The 2-second check only looks at folders (`check_for_changes` -> `folders_on_screen`, src/finder/mod.rs:1114-1168). A search is run again only when the query, scope, kind or a setting changes, on Refresh (mod.rs:1199-1207), or when the first scan ends (mod.rs:1503-1514). Operations done in fffinder merely drop rows that no longer exist (src/finder/trash.rs:368-371). So a file another program creates, renames or deletes after the search is missing or stale until Cmd+R, although the index already knows: it is watched, and `Engine::watch` streams exactly those changes (crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:1253-1287, used only by /v1/watch in src/server/mod.rs:510-570). The Save Smart Folder dialog promises results 'kept up to date' (src/finder/dialogs.rs:896), and Recents says 'Files you change appear here' (mod.rs:3251-3255) but is read once per visit (mod.rs:1043-1046).
proposal: While a name search or Recents is on screen, hold an `Engine::watch("", &[])` subscription in `Finder` (a new `search_watch: Option<Watch>` field, created off the UI thread from `run_search`/`load_listing` because subscribing takes index locks, dropped when the search ends or the location changes). In the existing 2-second tick (`check_for_changes`) drain `watch.events.try_recv()`, which never blocks. If a batch held a Created, Removed, Renamed or Rescan event and no search is running, call a new `pub fn index_changed(&mut self, cx)` that runs `run_search(false, cx)` again for a name search, or `load_listing(Vec::new(), true, cx)` for Recents. `rebuild_rows` already keeps the selection by path (mod.rs:1268-1269). Leave contents searches to Refresh (they can run up to the time limit). When `search.watch` is off or the scope uses a temporary index there is no subscription and nothing changes. Make the quiet rerun skip `self.searching = true` so the status-bar spinner does not blink.
original_test_plan: Deterministic headless test in tests/finder.rs: search `atlas`, select a row, write `atlas-two.txt` into the fixture, call `engine.rescan()` and `wait_ready`, call `f.index_changed(cx)`, `ui.settle()`, assert the new name is listed and the selection is unchanged; delete a listed file and assert it leaves the list the same way. Optional end-to-end test with a watching engine: add `watch: bool` to `Open` in tests/common/mod.rs:142-153 (the harness hard-codes `watch: false` at line 166) and retry with real sleeps the way tests/server.rs:293-317 does.
original_risks: Bursts of events (builds, downloads): the 2-second tick is the throttle and `search_gen` already discards stale responses. Real watcher timing can be flaky in CI, hence the deterministic test around `index_changed`. An extra subscription per searching tab is cheap but must be dropped on tab close (it unsubscribes in `Drop`, engine.rs:265-271). A quiet rerun must not trigger the scroll/selection reset proposed in results-scroll-reset.

verifier.claim_check:
The problem is real and not handled anywhere; the proposed mechanism has defects.

**Confirmed current behaviour**
- The 2-second tick only looks at folders: `check_for_changes` -> `folders_on_screen` -> `reload_changed` (src/finder/mod.rs:1114-1183). Window activation calls the same function (mod.rs:522-527).
- A search reruns only on query/scope/kind/setting changes (mod.rs:1323-1483, 1570-1612), on Refresh (mod.rs:1199-1207), on its own retry while indexing (mod.rs:1435-1457), and when the first scan ends (mod.rs:1503-1514).
- Operations done in fffinder only drop rows that no longer exist (src/finder/trash.rs:368-371).
- Recents is read in `load_listing` (mod.rs:1043-1046), so only on navigation, Refresh, scan end, or an in-app operation.
- `Engine::watch` (crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:1253-1287) is used only by `/v1/watch` (src/server/mod.rs:510-570).
- The dialog says "kept up to date" (src/finder/dialogs.rs:896). The manual defines that as "Clicking a Smart Folder runs the search again" (docs/manual.md:643), and its "Open folders refresh on their own" paragraph (manual.md:130) does not mention results. Nothing documents staleness as intended.
- No test pins the stale behaviour. The harness engine has `watch: false` (tests/common/mod.rs:166).
- fff dispatches watch events after the index is updated (fff-search-0.11.0/src/watcher/background_watcher.rs:558-687), so a rerun does see the change.

**Where the proposal is wrong**
1. Subscribing from `run_search`/`load_listing` often fails or covers only some roots. fff installs the watcher only after the post-scan pass (fff-search-0.11.0/src/scan.rs:233-271), which is the "finishing…" phase that can take minutes. Until then `SharedFilePicker::watch` returns `WatcherNotReady` (shared.rs:309-314). `Engine::watch` returns Ok if any one root subscribed (engine.rs:1277-1287). tests/server.rs:298-317 retries for this reason.
2. Nothing re-subscribes after `set_roots`/`set_search_settings` build new pickers (engine.rs:322-385). The held `Watch` keeps strong clones of the old pickers (engine.rs:260-263).
3. `check_for_changes` returns early when no folder is on screen (mod.rs:1126-1129). That is always the case in Recents, so a drain placed after it never runs there.
4. Recents is "modified in the last 30 days, newest first" (engine.rs:794-851). Its main trigger is Modified, which the proposal ignores.
5. "No subscription when the scope uses a temporary index" is false. `Engine::watch("")` subscribes to every root whatever the scope, and never to temporary indexes, which are watched too (engine.rs:495).
6. `searching` is the only guard against overlapping runs. Skipping it without a replacement lets each tick cancel the previous quiet rerun, since assigning `search_task` drops the old task.
verifier.implementation_notes:
Replace the per-Finder `Watch` and channel with a change counter owned by the engine. One subscription per index serves every tab, nothing queues up, there is no lifetime to manage, and the tick wiring becomes testable without a real watcher.

**crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs**
- Add `changes: Arc<ChangeCounts>` to `Engine`, with two `AtomicU64`s:
  - `listed`: bumped on Created, Removed, Renamed or Rescan.
  - `edited`: bumped on those plus Modified. Optionally skip paths with a dot-component or `Library`, as `recents()` does at engine.rs:829-833.
- Add `followed: Arc<AtomicBool>` to `RootIndex`. It is `Clone`, so the flag must be shared.
- Add `pub fn follow_changes(&self) -> bool`:
  - Return true at once when `!self.watch || !search_settings().watch`.
  - Otherwise, for every root and temporary index not yet followed, call `picker.watch("", WatchOptions::default(), cb)` and set `followed` on Ok.
  - Treat `WatcherNotReady` as "try again later". Return whether all are followed.
  - The callback captures only the `Arc<ChangeCounts>`, so there is no cycle. The subscription dies with the picker, so no unwatch is needed.
- Add `pub fn changes(&self) -> (u64, u64)`, atomic loads only, safe on the UI thread.
- Make `rescan()` bump both counters. An explicit rescan then refreshes results even when the 400 ms status poll misses a fast scan, and tests get a deterministic trigger.
- Leave `Engine::watch` and `/v1/watch` untouched.

**src/finder/mod.rs**
- New fields: `results_stamp: u64`, `recents_stamp: u64`, `following: bool`, `requerying: bool`.
- Add `check_index_for_changes(cx)` and call it in `check_for_changes` before the `checking_folders` and `shown.is_empty()` early returns (mod.rs:1123-1129).
- It acts only when a name search is on screen (`is_searching() && !search_contents`), or Recents is on screen with no search.
- Each tick, one at a time, call `engine.follow_changes()` through `cx.background_spawn`. It takes index and picker locks, as the comment at mod.rs:1436-1439 notes. It is cheap once everything is followed, and it also picks up new roots and temporary indexes.
- Split `run_search` into `start_search(debounce, quiet, cx)`:
  - Read `engine.changes().0` before spawning and store it as `results_stamp` on completion, so a change during the search is not lost.
  - When quiet, do not set `searching`; set `requerying` instead and clear it on completion.
  - Pass `quiet` through the retry at mod.rs:1451-1455.
  - If the new rows have the same paths in the same order, swap `results` without `selection_changed`.
- Tick rule for a name search: `!searching && !requerying && changes.0 != results_stamp` starts a quiet search.
- Tick rule for Recents: `changes.1 != recents_stamp` and no reload in flight calls `load_listing(Vec::new(), true, cx)`. Capture the stamp before the read.
  - The in-flight flag is required. The Recents branch blocks in `engine.wait_ready(60s)` (mod.rs:1044), and replacing `listing_task` does not unblock the background thread, so unguarded ticks during a rescan would pile up blocked threads.
- `rebuild_rows` already keeps the selection by path (mod.rs:1268-1269) and does not touch scroll. Do not route through `location_changed`.
- Leave contents searches to Refresh.

**Docs**
- docs/manual.md: extend the paragraph at line 130, the Smart Folder sentence at 643, and the `search.watch` row at 993 (off means results and Recents update on Refresh).
- CHANGELOG.md: add an entry under [Unreleased].
verifier.test_plan:
**Deterministic UI test** in tests/finder.rs, next to `searches_by_name_and_returns_to_browsing` (line 67). Model it on `folders_on_screen_show_what_other_programs_add` (tests/basics.rs:1168-1211).
- `Fixture::new`, `Ui::open`, `ui.press(&cmd("f"))`, `ui.type_text("atlas")`, `ui.select("Project Atlas.txt")`.
- Write `atlas-two.txt` into the fixture.
- Get the engine as tests/controls.rs:748 does: `ui.window(|_, cx| cx.global::<AppState>().engine.clone())`.
- Wait until `engine.status()` shows no `finishing`. A rescan requested during the post-scan pass is deferred, and `wait_ready` would then return early.
- Call `engine.rescan()` and assert `engine.wait_ready(20s)`.
- Trigger the tick with `ui.cx.executor().advance_clock(Duration::from_millis(2100))` then `ui.settle()`.
- Assert `ui.names()` contains `atlas-two.txt` and `ui.selected() == ["Project Atlas.txt"]`.
- Delete the file, rescan the same way, advance the clock, and assert the row is gone.
- Repeat for Recents: `ui.press(&cmd("shift-f"))`, write a file, rescan, advance the clock, assert it is listed.

This drives the real tick path, not just a helper, because `rescan()` bumps the counter. With the harness's `watch: false`, `follow_changes()` returns true at once, so existing tests are unaffected. A small `Ui::rescan()` helper in tests/common/mod.rs can wrap the wait, rescan, wait sequence.

**Engine unit tests** in the `tests` module of crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs (line 1778 onward):
- `rescan()` moves `changes()`.
- With a `watch: true` engine on a temp dir: loop `follow_changes()` until true, write a file, poll with real sleeps until `changes().0` moves and `search` finds it. Use the same retry style as tests/server.rs:293-317.

**Optional end-to-end test**: add `watch: bool` to `Open` (tests/common/mod.rs:142-153, hard-coded false at 166) and loop sleep, `advance_clock(2100ms)`, `settle` until the row appears.

I did not run cargo, per the read-only brief; the plan is from reading the code.
verifier.risks:
- **Background work while a search or Smart Folder stays open.** The default root is the whole home folder (crates/fffinder-core/src/config.rs:435). fff skips hidden directories, gitignored files and known cache folders for non-git roots (fff-search-0.11.0/src/walk/zlob.rs:21-22, src/ignore.rs), so noise is moderate, but visible folders that churn (Downloads, parts of ~/Library on macOS) can cause a rerun every 2 seconds. Mitigate by not rebuilding when the path list is unchanged; add a backoff if it shows up in profiles.
- **Rows move under the pointer** when a new match or a newly modified Recents file arrives. Finder does the same, but it is new behaviour here.
- **With a filter on**, a rerun whose paths changed starts a `nu` process (src/finder/filter.rs:96-109). Unchanged paths do not.
- **Rescan events fire when a rescan is triggered, not when it finishes.** The existing retry-while-indexing loop covers a running scan. A rescan deferred behind an active scan can leave results stale until the next event.
- **Nothing becomes live until the watcher is up**, which is after "finishing…". If the watcher never starts (Linux inotify limit, manual.md:100), `follow_changes` keeps returning false and behaviour stays as today.
- **Once followed, fff builds watch events for every batch** for the rest of the session. The overhead is small.
- **Real-watcher tests depend on inotify timing** and must retry, as tests/server.rs already does.

orchestrator_notes: Weigh the verifier's background-work risk carefully: nothing may add steady CPU or I/O while a search sits open on a large home folder. Prefer re-running the search when the index reports a change (debounced) over any new watching or polling.
